text: Nechtanebus is recorded under the heading of Nechtan, also called Elcmar, an Irish god or hero. The extract returns to one tale: the Boyne rises near the hillfort Sid Nechtain, a fairy mound, and Nechtan is sometimes equated with the god Nuada. Nechtan dwelt at Bru na Boinne with his wife Boand. Boand wanted the powerful Dagda and tricked her husband. The pair fled, and the Dagda kept the sun from moving for nine months, long enough for their child to arrive before Nechtan knew of the matter. The son, Aonghus Og, then deceived Nechtan into surrendering Bru na Boinne on the claim that he alone had no fairy palace.

okr.objective: Nechtanebus records the Irish god Nechtan and his loss of Bru na Boinne.
